prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Columbus. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Columbus Ohio for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — I just need two quick clarifying details so I give you accurate, useful names:

1) Which Columbus do you mean (Columbus, OH; Columbus, GA; Columbus, IN; etc.)?  
2) Any preferences: do you want an oral surgeon, a periodontist, or a general dentist who places implants? Do you have dental insurance, prefer sedation, or need a same-day/immediate-load implant or full-arch work?

If you tell me that, I’ll return a short list of specific practices near you (with why I recommend each one) plus the exact questions to ask when you call.

If you want to move forward right away without those details, here’s a quick, actionable plan you can use to find and call the right offices in any Columbus:

Which offices to call (general guidance)
- Board-certified oral & maxillofacial surgeons (OMS): Best for surgical complexity (bone grafting, impacted tooth removal, multiple implants, sedation/general anesthesia). Look for “board certified” or check AAOMS directory.
- Board-certified periodontists: Specialists in gums and implants, excellent for bone/gum grafting and implant placement around compromised gum tissue.
- Prosthodontists (when you need complex restoration or full-arch prostheses): They handle the crown/bridge and bite/occlusion planning for implants.
- High-volume private implant centers and university dental centers: Often have experience with many cases and modern technology (CBCT, guided surgery).

How to pick specific practices to call
- Look for these features in listings/reviews: board certification, years of implant experience, CBCT 3D imaging on site, in-house lab or a prosthodontist collaborator, sedation/IV option if you want it, published before/after patient photos, transparent pricing/financing.
- Check third-party sources: AAOMS (oral surgeons), American Academy of Periodontology (periodontists), ADA Find-a-Dentist, Google reviews, Healthgrades, RealSelf, and patient testimonials.

What to ask when you call (use this exact short script)
1. “Do you place dental implants? How many implant cases does your office do per month?” (high volume = more experience)  
2. “Who will place the implant — dentist, periodontist, or oral surgeon? Are they board-certified?”  
3. “Do you take cone beam CT (CBCT) scans in-office?”  
4. “Who will restore the implant crown — you or a separate prosthodontist?”  
5. “Do you do bone grafting/sinus lifts if needed?”  
6. “Do you offer sedation or IV anesthesia?”  
7. “What implant system do you use (Straumann, Nobel, Zimmer, etc.) and is there a warranty or guarantee?”  
8. “Can you give a rough cost range for a single implant with crown and any common additional procedures?”  
9. “Do you have before/after photos and patient references I can see?”  
10. “How long is the typical timeline from placement to final crown in your practice?”

Red flags when you call
- Vague answers about who does the surgery or what implant system is used.  
- No CBCT for implant planning.  
- No written estimate or unwillingness to explain steps/timeline.  
- Pushy sales tactics or “lifetime guarantee” claims that aren’t backed in writing.

If you tell me which Columbus and any preferences/insurance, I’ll give you a tailored list of 4–6 practices to call (names, why each is recommended, and who to ask for).
